help.intro: A three-minute checkpoint on the first half of this module, in your own AI assistant with voice on: single things you did yesterday, one sentence at a time. The tutor asks 'Was hast du gestern gemacht?' and follow-ups; you answer in the Perfekt. It is listening for three decisions per sentence — haben or sein, and the participle at the end — plus the participle's form (gegessen not geesst, gefahren not gefahrt). Answer in complete sentences, and let the tutor keep its corrections for the report.
help.tips[0].title: One sentence, two verbs
help.tips[0].text: Every answer has a helper at 2 and a participle at the end: Ich habe gearbeitet. Ich bin ins Kino gegangen. Two words, two positions, nothing in between the helper and the subject.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Yesterday I worked late and came home late.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: On Saturday I met my friends.
help.tips[0].check.why: The helper habe sits in position 2 and the participle gebacken goes to the very end.
help.tips[1].title: Movement? Then bin.
help.tips[1].text: gehen, fahren, kommen, laufen, fliegen, aufstehen → bin. Everything else → habe. Decide before you open your mouth.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: I got up at eight. I had breakfast.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: I went into town by bus and did some shopping.
help.tips[1].check.q: Am Montag ____ ich nach Köln geflogen.
help.tips[1].check.why: fliegen is movement from A to B, so it takes bin.
help.tips[1].visual.root.q: Did you move from A to B, or change state?
help.remember[0]: Helper at 2, participle last — say the participle, then stop.
help.hook: Tell someone what you did yesterday, one clean sentence at a time: the right helper, and the participle last.
speaking.topic: Single things I did yesterday, one sentence at a time.
speaking.practisePoints[0]: Perfekt with haben: the most common past in speech
speaking.practisePoints[1]: Perfekt with sein for movement: gegangen, gefahren, gekommen
speaking.material: Ask at least two questions that need a movement verb with sein (Wohin bist du gestern gegangen / gefahren? Wann bist du nach Hause gekommen?) and at least two that need haben (Was hast du gegessen? Was hast du am Abend gemacht?).
